import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

marker.step_source:
head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

## Summary

Completed bead **sase-lh.2** (store phase of the `sase-lh` background-tasks-to-procs epic): moved `src/sase/tasks` → `src/sase/procs` via `git mv`, renamed `BackgroundTask`→`Proc`/`task_id`→`proc_id` and all related symbols throughout, added `src/sase/procs/_migration.py` for the marker-guarded on-disk `~/.sase/tasks`→`~/.sase/procs` migration, renamed the config key to `procs.history_limit` (with `tasks.history_limit` kept as a legacy alias), and updated every call site plus `tools/validate_sase_core_rs`.

While verifying with `just check`, I found and fixed 5 real regressions the prior work had introduced: two test mocks with a stale `task_id` attribute instead of `proc_id`, a stale binding-name assertion in the `validate_sase_core_rs` tool test, a missing exemption entry for the new directory-operation audit gate, and — most notably — a scope leak where `ProcRefError`'s message text and `"proc killed"` status wording had already flipped from "task" to "proc" inconsistently across tests. Since displayed/status text is explicitly the job of the epic's later `labels` phase, I reverted that wording back to "task" and fixed the one test (`test_procs_facade.py`) that had baked in the premature wording.

`just check` (lint gates + full escalated test suite, ~29,766 tests) passed clean on the final run. Two earlier full runs each hit exactly one unrelated, non-reproducing flaky test under heavy concurrent multi-workspace load (confirmed passing standalone); I recorded that as a `PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP` note on the bead. The bead is closed and the changes are committed and pushed to `master`.
